title: Mifepristone REMS pharmacy certification and the certified pharmacy's program requirements
rule_summary: FDA states that the Mifepristone REMS Program sets forth the requirements that must be followed for prescribing and dispensing mifepristone for medical termination of pregnancy through ten weeks gestation. FDA also states that under the program mifepristone must be prescribed by certified prescribers and must be dispensed by or under the supervision of a certified prescriber or by a certified pharmacy on a prescription issued by a certified prescriber. The approved Mifepristone REMS Program document (single shared system for mifepristone 200 mg; most recent modification 09/2025) states as a goal ensuring that mifepristone is only dispensed by or under the supervision of certified prescribers, or by certified pharmacies on prescriptions issued by certified prescribers, and requires that pharmacies that dispense mifepristone be specially certified. To become certified a pharmacy must be able to receive Prescriber Agreement Forms by email and fax, be able to ship mifepristone using a shipping service that provides tracking information, designate an authorized representative to carry out the certification process on behalf of the pharmacy, and ensure that the authorized representative oversees implementation and compliance by reviewing the Prescribing Information and completing a Pharmacy Agreement Form. By signing that form the authorized representative agrees that the pharmacy will put processes and procedures in place to: verify that the prescriber is certified by confirming that the prescriber's completed Prescriber Agreement Form was received with the prescription or is on file with the pharmacy; dispense mifepristone such that it is delivered to the patient within 4 calendar days of the date the pharmacy receives the prescription, except that for a patient who will receive the drug more than 4 calendar days after that date the pharmacy confirms the appropriateness of dispensing with the prescriber and documents the prescriber's decision; record in the patient's record the NDC and lot number from each package dispensed; track and verify receipt of each shipment; dispense mifepristone in its package as supplied by the Mifepristone Sponsor; report any patient deaths to the prescriber, including the NDC and lot number, remind the prescriber of the obligation to report deaths to the Mifepristone Sponsor that provided the mifepristone, and notify that Sponsor that the pharmacy submitted a report of death to the prescriber; not distribute, transfer, loan or sell mifepristone except to certified prescribers or other locations of the pharmacy; maintain records of Prescriber Agreement Forms, of dispensing and shipping, and of all processes and procedures including compliance with them; maintain the identity of the patient and prescriber as confidential, limiting access to those personnel necessary to dispense mifepristone under the program or as necessary for payment and/or insurance purposes; train all relevant staff on the program requirements; and comply with audits carried out by the Mifepristone Sponsors or a third party acting on their behalf. The Mifepristone Sponsors must de-certify pharmacies that do not maintain compliance, verify annually that the name and contact information of the pharmacy's authorized representative are current and, if different, require the pharmacy to recertify with the new authorized representative, and audit certified pharmacies within 180 calendar days after the pharmacy places its first order and annually thereafter for certified pharmacies that ordered in the previous 12 months; distributors must ship mifepristone only to certified pharmacies or locations identified by certified prescribers. FDA states that the January 3, 2023 modification removed the in-person dispensing requirement and added pharmacy certification, that it removed the restriction that did not allow mifepristone to be dispensed by retail pharmacies, that any pharmacy that meets the program requirements is eligible for certification, and that under the program mifepristone may be dispensed in person or by mail.
exam_relevance: Tests the certified pharmacy's own obligations: verifying the prescriber's certification, the 4-calendar-day delivery period and its prescriber-confirmation route, NDC and lot recording, and the limits on moving stock.

numeric_facts.fact: period within which a certified pharmacy dispenses mifepristone so that it is delivered to the patient
numeric_facts.conditions: from the date the pharmacy receives the prescription; for delivery after that period the pharmacy confirms appropriateness with the prescriber and documents the prescriber's decision

numeric_facts.fact: first Mifepristone Sponsor audit of a certified pharmacy
numeric_facts.conditions: after the pharmacy places its first order of mifepristone; annually thereafter for certified pharmacies that ordered in the previous 12 months

exceptions: A patient who will receive mifepristone more than 4 calendar days after the pharmacy receives the prescription may be dispensed to once the pharmacy has confirmed the appropriateness of dispensing with the prescriber and documented the prescriber's decision.
A certified pharmacy may distribute, transfer, loan or sell mifepristone to certified prescribers or to other locations of the pharmacy, and to no one else.
common_confusions: Assuming a retail pharmacy cannot dispense mifepristone; FDA states that the January 2023 modification removed that restriction and that any pharmacy meeting the program requirements is eligible for certification.
Treating the 4-calendar-day period as an absolute bar; beyond it the pharmacy confirms appropriateness with the prescriber and documents the prescriber's decision.
Dispensing on a prescription without confirming the prescriber's certification; the pharmacy verifies that the completed Prescriber Agreement Form was received with the prescription or is on file.
Believing the program still requires in-person dispensing; FDA states that mifepristone may be dispensed in person or by mail.
